cards.design_implication: If validating this specific tomography protocol, the experimental design should include a calibration step using multislice simulations matched to the refined atomic model to quantify reconstruction precision for different atomic species.
does_not_establish: Generalizable precision limits for atomic electron tomography across all material systems.
Absolute accuracy of atomic positions without the assumption that the initial reconstruction is structurally sound.
cards.evidence_excerpt: From the experimental 3D atomic model, we combined multislice simulations with scanning AET to estimate the 3D precision of the method to be 4 pm, 15 pm, 6 pm and 15 pm for the Mo, S, W and Se atoms, respectively (see supplementary materials).
limitations: This precision estimate applies specifically to the described sAET workflow on a MoS2-WSe2 interface using the reported instrument settings.
The estimate is derived from simulation comparison against the experimental model, not independent ground-truth measurement.
cards.statement: The 3D precision of the atomic coordinates for Mo, S, W, and Se atoms was estimated to be 4 pm, 15 pm, 6 pm, and 15 pm, respectively, by combining multislice simulations with scanning atomic electron tomography (sAET).

cards.design_implication: When adapting this approach to other heterostructures, the design must account for material-specific lattice mismatch and the potential formation of interface defects such as vacancies or bond distortions.
does_not_establish: A universal defect formation energy or strain profile for all 2D heterostructures.
That all material pairs with this specific mismatch will exhibit the same type of atomic-scale ripples.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Since the lattice constant of WSe<sub>2</sub> is 5.53% larger than that of MoS<sub>2</sub> (6), the lattice mismatch must be accommodated by significant crystal defects at the interface.
limitations: The findings regarding defect accommodation are specific to the 5.53% lattice mismatch of this particular heterojunction pair.
Results may not directly transfer to heterostructures with smaller lattice mismatches or different interface configurations.
cards.statement: The study demonstrates the method on a specific epitaxial MoS2-WSe2 lateral heterojunction interface, where lattice mismatch was accommodated by crystal defects and strain.

cards.design_implication: If designing thermal barrier interfaces using similar materials, the thermal transport model should consider the mismatch in PDOS between the two materials as a primary scattering mechanism at the interface.
does_not_establish: A precise quantitative value for thermal boundary resistance based solely on this PDOS mismatch.
That PDOS mismatch is the sole or dominant factor in thermal resistance for all heterojunctions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: In the case of the ${ \mathrm { M o S } } _ { 2 } { \mathrm { - } } { \mathrm { W S e } } _ { 2 }$ heterojunction, the difference in PDOS, suggests several optical phonon modes in WSe<sub>2</sub> cannot scatter into MoS<sub>2</sub> while simultaneously conserving their energy and momentum.
limitations: This is a mechanistic suggestion based on the calculated PDOS difference in the specific heterojunction studied.
Other scattering mechanisms (e.g., boundary scattering, anharmonicity) are not explicitly quantified in this excerpt.
cards.statement: The authors propose that the difference in phonon density of states (PDOS) between MoS2 and WSe2 prevents certain optical phonon modes in WSe2 from scattering into MoS2 while conserving energy and momentum, which impedes heat transport.
